title: Width, height, min/max sizing
learningObjectives: Explain width, height, min/max sizing and use it in a practical layout.

understand.concept: width and height set preferred dimensions; min-width, max-width, min-height, and max-height constrain them. Percentages depend on the containing block, and percentage heights need a definite containing-block height to resolve as expected.
understand.whyItMatters: Fixed dimensions can cause overflow when content grows or the viewport narrows. Prefer flexible sizing and use minimum/maximum constraints to protect layout and readability.
understand.analogy: A container has a target size but also needs safe limits, like a shelf that can expand or stop before becoming too narrow.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy supports intuition; browser layout follows the CSS formatting and sizing rules.

explain.narrative: The panel occupies up to 90% of its containing block and stops growing at 34rem.

examples.code: This panel has a flexible width and a maximum size.
examples.explanation: The panel occupies up to 90% of its containing block and stops growing at 34rem.

questions.prompt: Which property sets an upper limit on an element's width?
questions.explanation: max-width prevents the used width from exceeding the specified limit.

questions.prompt: What is a useful way to verify the effect of a CSS sizing rule?
options: Inspect computed styles and test different content sizes
Assume the declared width includes every box layer

questions.explanation: Computed styles and varied content reveal how the browser resolves sizing rules.
